title: The shared kitchen

context.situation: You share a flat with another person. The kitchen needs cleaning. Both of you independently decide whether to Clean or Leave it.
context.players: Two people: you (Roommate A) and the person you share with (Roommate B).
context.preferences: Each of you wants a clean kitchen but would rather not do the work. Best for you: B cleans and you don’t. Next best: you both clean. Then: nobody cleans. Worst: you clean alone while B leaves it. B sees it the same way from B’s side.
context.choices: Each person has the same two options: Clean or Leave it.
context.learnerControls: Only your own choice: Clean or Leave it.
context.opponentControls: Only B’s own choice: Clean or Leave it. Neither of you can force the other.
context.knownUnknown: You know both options and how each combination feels to each of you. You don’t know what B will do; B is deciding at the same time and cares about the same kind of things you do.
context.timing: Simultaneous: you both decide at once, and neither sees the other’s choice before deciding.
context.payoffMeaning: Each outcome gets a number for each person: how good it is for that person on a 0–5 scale. Higher is better. Only the order and size within this situation matter; the numbers are not money.
context.task: First predict what Roommate B will choose and say how confident you are. Then make your own choice. It locks in, and you will see what happened.

opponentPolicy.description: Roommate B’s choice was drawn by a fixed rule written into this exercise: Leave it 7 times in 10, Clean 3 times in 10. Each attempt has its own seed, so a draw can be replayed exactly. Your decision is never graded on this draw.
opponentPolicy.rationale: B mostly leaves it (Leave it is better for B whatever A does) but sometimes cleans, as real people often do. The mix makes both outcomes in B’s column appear across attempts, so the learner meets the difference between a good decision and a lucky or unlucky outcome. It is consistent with what A is told: A does not know B’s choice; B decides at the same time and cares about the same kind of things.

prompts.predict: What do you predict Roommate B will choose?
prompts.confidence: How confident are you that Roommate B will choose {prediction}?
prompts.decideNote: Roommate B is deciding at the same time and won’t see your choice. Your choice locks in: you can’t change it afterwards.

outcomes.clean|clean: You both cleaned. The work was shared and the kitchen is spotless. A fair, decent result for each of you.
outcomes.clean|leave: You cleaned while B left it. The kitchen is clean, but you did all the work and B enjoyed it for free.
outcomes.leave|clean: You left it and B cleaned. You get a clean kitchen without lifting a finger; B did all the work.
outcomes.leave|leave: You both left it. Nobody did any work, and the kitchen stays a mess for both of you.

matrix.intro: Here is the whole situation as a table of every possible combination. It is a model of the story you just played.
howToRead: Each cell is one combination of both choices.
In each cell the first number is yours (Roommate A) and the second is Roommate B’s.
You chose a row. B chose a column. Together they landed in the highlighted cell.

questions.prompt: If Roommate B chooses Clean, which is better for you?
If Roommate B chooses Leave it, which is better for you?
Is there one action that gives you more whatever Roommate B does?

feedback.bestReplyIncorrect: Not quite. {lines} So {best} is better for you.
feedback.bestReplyTie: {lines} Both are equally good for you here.
feedback.dominantCorrect: Yes. {lines} {dominant} gives you more whatever B does.
feedback.dominantIncorrect: Not quite. {lines} {dominant} gives you more whatever B does.
feedback.noneCorrect: Right. {lines} Which is better depends on what B does.
feedback.noneIncorrect: Not quite. {lines} No single action is better whatever B does; it depends on B.

closingNote: {dominant} is better for you either way, and the same holds for B. Yet if both of you reason this way, you each get {mutualYou} instead of {betterYou}.
